_meta.semantics: covers_syllabus_refs is an index of the objectives a stage is principally associated with; coverage is claimed only through _syllabus_items + covers_items, and only as far as coverage_check.py confirms.

_items_source.document: AQA GCSE Spanish (8692) specification, first teaching September 2024: themes 3.1, grammar 3.2, vocabulary 3.3
_items_source.version: Specification for first teaching from September 2024, linked from aqa.org.uk/8692, itemised 2026-09-27
_items_source.numbering: AQA numbers the three themes and their three topics each (3.1.1-3.1.3 per theme) but presents the content under each topic, and the whole of 3.2 Grammar, as unnumbered bullet lists. This course codes the eighteen topic-content items by theme.topic and a letter in AQA's own bullet order (e.g. T1.1a, T1.1b for Theme 1 Topic 1), and codes the sixteen grammar points G1-G16 in the specification's own order (Foundation content first, then the Higher-tier additions folded into the same numbered point where AQA presents them together), plus five items (LIS.1, SPK.1, SPK.2, RDG.1, WRT.1) for the exam-skill content of each of the four papers, which AQA sets out in its scheme of assessment rather than as numbered subject content.

_syllabus_items.title: Nouns: gender, plural formation, infinitives as nouns
Articles and demonstrative, indefinite and possessive adjectives
Adjective agreement, position, and comparatives/superlatives
Ser and estar
Adverbs, including -mente formation, and prepositions
Subject, direct/indirect object and reflexive pronouns
Interrogative, relative, neuter demonstrative and possessive pronouns; pronouns after prepositions
Negation
Present indicative, present continuous, modal, reflexive and impersonal verbs
Preterite tense, including stem-changing -ir verbs
Imperfect and imperfect continuous
Present perfect
Future (ir a + infinitive and the inflectional future) and conditional
Imperative
Present subjunctive (common Higher-tier uses), acabar de, seguir/llevar + gerund, passive voice, desde hace + present
Derivational morphology for reading: diminutives, superlatives, -mente, -idad, -able
Listening strategies and dictation
Speaking: role-play and reading aloud
Speaking: photo card discussion and general conversation
Reading strategies and translation into English
Writing tasks, translation into Spanish and extended writing
